correctness.rationale: For any word with \(k\) right visits, both derivative matrices are signed monomial, with permutation addition by \(k\) modulo \(M\). Its \(\gcd(k,M)\) weighted cycles each have length \(M/g\) and sign \((-1)^{k/g}\). When \(M\nmid k\), that degree is at least two; in degree two the sign is necessarily negative because \(\gcd(k/g,2)=1\), and in every higher degree a nonzero real pure-power equation has complex roots. When \(M\mid k\), all cycles have length one and all roots are real. The polynomial products each have positive magnitudes powers of 2, with total exponent \(n\) from the Jacobian determinant magnitude \(2^n\). Saiki–Takahasi–Yorke prove bijection of non-all-left length-n words and nontrivial iterate-fixed points; the binomial residue count and roots-of-unity filter give exact numbers and exponential estimate. Independent exact-rational finite checks verified every word for dimensions 2..6 and lengths 1..6, without extrapolating finite tests to an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full relevant source text supplies only the divisible residue real-spectrum sufficient condition, the adjacent residue nonreal-spectrum sufficient conditions, and asymptotic lower bounds (Lemmas 2.2–2.3, Proposition 2.7). The source never classifies the intermediate residues that exist in dimensions \(M\ge4\), nor states the exact spectral counts or limiting proportion \((M-1)/M\). The new signed-cycle argument exhausts those cases. A separate 2024 heterochaos baker-map study uses a different piecewise map and different spectral observables. Targeted searches of indexed mathematical findings and web literature did not identify an equivalent claim; an unindexed monomial-matrix treatment remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The natural relative abundance of periodic points with complex versus entirely real multipliers was explicitly considered but previously bounded only from below. The result yields an exact dimension-dependent limiting frequency \(1-1/M\), substantially sharper than the cited \(2/M\) lower bound when \(M\ge4\), and resolves previously unclassified intermediate twist residues. The signed-cycle factorization explains spectral structure rather than merely recomputing a known binomial table. The invariant is intrinsic to the original model and is meaningful for periodic-point statistics of vortex-like dynamics.
